attribution: Russian Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR), per US/UK government and Mandiant/Microsoft reporting.
why_relevant: APT29 is the nation-state actor whose tradecraft most closely matches Tycoon2FA: identity-first, cloud/Microsoft 365 focused, built around stealing authentication material and bypassing MFA. Comparing the two shows a commodity PhaaS kit and an elite state actor share the same identity-attack core.

techniques.name: Phishing: Spearphishing Link
techniques.apt29_use: Spearphishing links to zip/HTML payloads; 2023-2024 campaigns used Microsoft Teams and device-code phishing lures.

techniques.name: Phishing: Spearphishing Attachment
techniques.apt29_use: Malicious attachments (e.g. LNK, ISO, exploit docs) to initial victims.

techniques.name: Multi-Factor Authentication Request Generation
techniques.apt29_use: MFA 'push bombing' - repeated prompts until the victim approves one.
techniques.our_detection: related to our T1111 coverage; many-prompts pattern = new hunt idea

techniques.name: Steal Web Session Cookie
techniques.apt29_use: Stole session cookies/tokens to access mailboxes without a password.

techniques.name: Forge Web Credentials: Web Cookies
techniques.apt29_use: Forged SAML tokens ('Golden SAML') and OWA cookies from a stolen signing key to bypass MFA.
techniques.our_detection: not covered - AD FS / token-signing-cert monitoring (future work)

techniques.name: Use Alternate Auth Material: Web Session Cookie
techniques.apt29_use: Reused stolen session cookies to authenticate as the victim.

techniques.name: Use Alternate Auth Material: Application Access Token
techniques.apt29_use: Used OAuth application access tokens to reach cloud resources and mail.
techniques.our_detection: not covered - OAuth token / app monitoring (future work)

techniques.name: Account Manipulation: Device Registration
techniques.apt29_use: Enrolled attacker-controlled devices in compromised tenants for mailbox sync and durable access.

techniques.name: Account Manipulation: Additional Cloud Credentials
techniques.apt29_use: Added credentials/secrets to existing OAuth apps and service principals.
techniques.our_detection: not covered - service-principal credential-add auditing (future work)

techniques.name: Account Manipulation: Additional Email Delegate Permissions
techniques.apt29_use: Granted themselves delegated mailbox permissions to read others' mail.
techniques.our_detection: not covered - mailbox delegation auditing (future work)

techniques.name: Account Manipulation: Additional Cloud Roles
techniques.apt29_use: Assigned admin roles (e.g. Global Admin) to accounts/service principals they controlled.

techniques.name: Account Discovery: Cloud Account
techniques.apt29_use: Enumerated Azure AD / Entra ID accounts and directory objects.

techniques.name: Email Collection: Remote Email Collection
techniques.apt29_use: Collected email from mailboxes in Azure AD tenants and Exchange (incl. the 2024 Microsoft corporate-mailbox breach).

techniques.name: Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts
techniques.apt29_use: Logged in with stolen valid cloud credentials/tokens, blending into normal traffic.
techniques.our_detection: hunt H0 IOC sweep + CAR analytic (Weeks 5, 7)

techniques.name: Supply Chain Compromise: Software Supply Chain
techniques.apt29_use: SolarWinds Orion compromise (2020) - trojanised updates to thousands of organisations.
techniques.our_detection: not covered - nation-state capability beyond a PhaaS kit

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over Asymmetric Encrypted Non-C2 Protocol
techniques.apt29_use: Exfiltrated password-protected archives over HTTPS to attacker infrastructure.
techniques.our_detection: related to our T1567 egress controls (Week 8)
